title: Evaluating the Impact of Community Oversight for Managing Mobile Privacy and Security
venue: USENIX Symposium on Usable Privacy and Security (SOUPS) 2023
extended_summary:
This paper investigates whether community-based oversight can help people manage mobile privacy and security together. The authors focus on the problem that users often struggle to understand app permissions and privacy risks on their own, and instead rely on advice from trusted peers. To address this, they propose and evaluate a community oversight model that emphasizes transparency, awareness, trust, individual participation, and community participation.

The intervention is CO-oPS (Community Oversight of Privacy and Security), an Android app that lets members of a self-selected community view one another’s installed apps and granted permissions, send direct feedback, discuss privacy concerns, and receive weekly educational tips. The app also includes controls for hiding selected apps and links to Android settings so users can change permissions. The study used a four-week mixed-method longitudinal field design with 101 participants in 22 self-formed groups in the United States.

Participants ranged from teens to older adults, though most were young adults. Communities were mainly composed of family members, friends, coworkers, and acquaintances. Data sources included pre- and post-surveys, weekly surveys, app usage logs, and follow-up interviews. The authors found increases in transparency, awareness, trust, individual participation, community participation, self-efficacy, and collective efficacy; community belonging did not change significantly. They conclude that community oversight can support real-world privacy and security co-management, but effectiveness depends on trust, relationship closeness, and differences in technical expertise.

identified_tools.name: GenAI (General)
identified_tools.description: A generic AI system category; however, this paper does not study generative AI or any instructional-coaching tool. It studies a mobile app for community oversight of privacy and security (CO-oPS).
identified_tools.use_case: Not an AI tool study for instructional coaching or lesson plan feedback; the paper evaluates the CO-oPS mobile app for peer/community oversight of mobile privacy and security decisions.

quality_tier_rationale: This is a mixed-methods field study with surveys, logs, and interviews, but it does not evaluate an AI instructional tool. The empirical design is clear, yet it is outside the requested AI-in-education use case.
impact_tier_rationale: The paper reports meaningful changes in privacy/security behaviors and perceptions, but not educational AI outcomes. Since no instructional coaching or lesson-feedback system is studied, impact for the target domain is not established.
